children: Indian government bonds could see mild gains in opening trades on Tuesday, tracking a decline in crude oil prices, but major moves are unlikely on concerns over further interest rate hikes in India and the US.
The benchmark 6.94% 2036 bond (IN069436G=CC) yield is expected to move between 7.29% and 7.35%, according to a private-bank trader, after ending at 7.3169% on Monday.
"Bulls may try their hand today as well, but the broader sentiment remains of caution," the trader said.
Oil prices eased, with the benchmark Brent crude contract dipping over 3%, as signs of recovering oil flows through the Strait of Hormuz reinforced expectations of a supply surplus.

The global oil market will return to a surplus in the fourth quarter of this year, the International Energy Agency said on Friday, as exports from the Middle East recover faster than global oil demand despite continued attacks on shipping.
The move in oil prices is crucial for an import-dependent India, as it impacts the local currency, inflation trajectory and government finances.

Market participants have factored in another rate hike by the Reserve Bank of India in early December after India's retail inflation accelerated to 6.09% in October, rising above the central bank's 6% tolerance level for the first time in two years.
Some are also expecting a larger-than-usual 50 basis point rise at a time when the Federal Reserve may also go down that path.

Treasury yields have been trending upward after stronger-than-expected October consumer price data and hawkish commentary from some Fed members prompted markets to eye a 50-basis-point rise on December 9, the odds of which currently stand at around 5%, per the CME FedWatch tool.
Traders will focus on debt supply as Indian states raise 233 billion rupees ($2.48 billion) through the sale of debt later in the day.
Overnight index swap rates may see mild receiving interest after ending little changed in the previous session.
The one-year (INR1YMIBROIS=CC) rate ended at 6.50%, while the two-year rate (INR2YMIBROIS=CC) ended at 6.51%. The liquid five-year (INR5YMIBROIS=CC) rate settled at 6.59%.
